subject.title: Multibulto FEDEX para consolidados pesados (prep-centers tipo ZoomBooks)

question: Should the remaining prep-center FEDEX workflow be implemented now as staged fulfillment work, and should prep-centers be identified by recipient/address ShipMatrix rules or by a more explicit B2B/prep-center marker?
rationale: The issue is valid but crosses carrier-routing data model, operations configuration, batch-label policy, and packing UX; automation should not choose the long-term prep-center matching contract on its own.

options.title: Stage the fulfillment implementation
options.body: Add recipient/address matching or an approved explicit prep-center marker first, then batch-skip behavior and packing self-service FEDEX generation in follow-up PRs.

options.title: Keep as backlog feature
options.body: Leave the current manual Spring-to-FEDEX switch in place and keep the broader automatic prep-center workflow queued until operations prioritizes it.

options.title: Narrow to routing only
options.body: Only add a ShipMatrix criterion now and defer packing self-service, accepting that heavy consolidations may still need manual handling.

recommendation.title: Stage the fulfillment implementation
recommendation.body: Add recipient/address matching or an approved explicit prep-center marker first, then batch-skip behavior and packing self-service FEDEX generation in follow-up PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: JavierHamelyn has the strongest recent history across ShipMatrix selection, carrier-resolution precedence, and manual carrier switching.
